layers.authority: Public security and border control bodies, Yunnan Province
layers.process: Everyone entering or leaving Yunnan's border areas (the counties that touch Myanmar, Laos or Vietnam) must carry valid identity papers and accept border checks at checkpoints on the roads in. Without valid papers, or refusing a check, a person may not enter or leave the border area. Temporary checkpoints can be set up for security, counter-terrorism or anti-drug work.

sources.title: Yunnan Province Border Management Regulations (云南省边境管理条例), passed 15 December 2016, in force 1 January 2017
sources.authority: Standing Committee of the Yunnan Provincial People's Congress (text hosted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China)

zone-requirements.note: The regulation does not name a separate pass for foreigners; whether a border management zone pass is needed for a given place is set nationally and locally and was not checked.

laws.rule: In Yunnan, cross the national border only at a designated port or border crossing, with valid papers, and accept the border check. Crossing elsewhere with valid papers: a warning and a possible fine of CNY 50 (about A$11). Avoiding a border check or using forged or borrowed papers: papers taken, a warning and a possible fine of CNY 100 to 300 (about A$21 to A$64). AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = CNY 4.6877).

Entering or leaving a Yunnan border area without valid papers or refusing a check, and not stopping when told: a warning and a possible fine of CNY 100 to 300 (about A$21 to A$64). Refusing to cooperate with a border check or seriously disrupting a checkpoint: a warning and a possible fine of CNY 500 to 1,500 (about A$107 to A$320). AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = CNY 4.6877).
